**2B.9 Research Note: Sheikh Hasina in 2024**

Overall read: **mostly negative**. I found only one weak post-hoc accountability signal. The main 2024 record shows Hasina’s government blaming opponents, maintaining coercive measures, and then facing UN/HRW findings of severe abuse. I found **no credible evidence** that she meaningfully accepted responsibility while the violence was unfolding or that she acknowledged later evidence contradicting the stated justification.

**Accepted claims**

- **Former Bangladesh PM Hasina demands probe into July ‘killings and vandalism’**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** August 13, 2024
  - **URL:** [https://theprint.in/world/former-bangladesh-pm-hasina-demands-probe-into-july-killings-and-vandalism/2222256/](https://theprint.in/world/former-bangladesh-pm-hasina-demands-probe-into-july-killings-and-vandalism/2222256/)
  - **Summary:** After fleeing, Hasina called for an investigation into the killings and vandalism. This is the closest accountability signal I found, but it is post-hoc and does not show acceptance of responsibility while the abuse was happening.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.9, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh PM Hasina blames opposition for violence, curfew to remain**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** July 22, 2024
  - **URL:** [https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-calm-a-day-after-top-court-scrapped-some-job-quotas-3528153](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/bangladesh-calm-a-day-after-top-court-scrapped-some-job-quotas-3528153)
  - **Summary:** Hasina kept the curfew in place and blamed political opponents for the violence. This is the opposite of accepting responsibility for civilian harm or for the failure of the government response.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.9, 2B.1, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh: Türk decries government crackdown, urges respect for international human rights standards**
  - **Publisher:** United Nations / OHCHR
  - **Date:** July 26, 2024
  - **URL:** [https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/275065-bangladesh-t%C3%BCrk-decries-government-crackdown-urges-respect-international-human-rights)
  - **Summary:** The UN said more than 170 people had been killed and warned that internet shutdowns increase impunity. This strongly undercuts any claim that the government accepted responsibility for illegal conduct or civilian harm.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.9, 2B.4, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Exclusive-Bangladesh army refused to suppress protest, sealing Hasina's fate**
  - **Publisher:** Reuters
  - **Date:** August 6, 2024
  - **URL:** [https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/exclusivebangladesh-army-refused-to-suppress-protest-sealing-hasinas-fate-3558302](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/exclusivebangladesh-army-refused-to-suppress-protest-sealing-hasinas-fate-3558302)
  - **Summary:** Reuters reported the army would not fire on civilians to enforce Hasina’s curfew. This suggests the government was willing to rely on lethal coercion and did not publicly take responsibility for that failure.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.9, 2B.4, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **Bangladesh: Back UN Investigation into Grave Abuses**
  - **Publisher:** Human Rights Watch
  - **Date:** August 26, 2024
  - **URL:** [https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/26/bangladesh-back-un-investigation-grave-abuses](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/08/26/bangladesh-back-un-investigation-grave-abuses)
  - **Summary:** HRW said the crackdown was the deadliest in Bangladesh’s recent history, with at least 440 killed, citing excessive force by law enforcement and violence by Awami League-affiliated youth groups. This is strong evidence of civilian harm and a failure to accept accountability.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.9, 2B.5, 2B.4, 1B.8, 1B.5

- **UN Fact-Finding Team Issues Call for Submissions**
  - **Publisher:** United Nations in Bangladesh / OHCHR
  - **Date:** September 16, 2024
  - **URL:** [https://bangladesh.un.org/en/278741-un-fact-finding-team-issues-call-submissions](https://bangladesh.un.org/en/278741-un-fact-finding-team-issues-call-submissions)
  - **Summary:** The UN opened a fact-finding process on alleged violations from July 1 to August 15, 2024. That strongly corroborates that the government’s stated justification did not resolve the accountability problem and that serious allegations remained unresolved.
  - **Question IDs:** 2B.9, 2B.4, 1B.8, 1B.5

**Synthesis**

- **Weak positive:** Hasina’s post-fleeing demand for a probe is the only visible accountability signal.
- **Strong negative:** During the crisis she blamed opponents, maintained coercive measures, and then faced credible external findings of excessive force, deaths, and impunity.
- Best-supported conclusion: **No, Hasina did not meaningfully accept accountability for military failures, civilian harm, or illegal conduct in 2024; her only pro-accountability move was late and limited.**

**Search gap**

- I searched for evidence that she:
  - accepted blame,
  - acknowledged civilian harm,
  - corrected false justifications,
  - or disciplined forces after later contrary evidence emerged.
- I found **no reliable 2024 evidence** of that behavior.
